governing_intent: Provide a fail-closed, read-only doctor gate that refuses autonomous work unless the configured profile has positively evidenced configuration, integration, persistence, and execution readiness.
summary: PY-09 is bounded around one coherent pre-autonomy validation capability. It specifies hard-required checks, outcome semantics, exit codes, sanitization, non-mutation, integration with run, and executable CLI-level proof without requiring unresolved Founder or architecture decisions.
implementation_unknowns: Define adapter-level error classification that consistently distinguishes FAIL from UNAVAILABLE while preserving sanitized causes.
Choose check-provider interfaces and fixture/double arrangements for each predecessor-owned capability.
Use a temporary owned local probe or equivalent non-mutating Git capability evidence for worktree and publication readiness.
Exercise the reserved WARNING aggregation path in a test-only result fixture, since Wave 1 defines no advisory doctor checks.
verification_assessment: Strong and mechanically observable: real CLI subprocess invocation, retained exit statuses, pass/fail coverage for every check, explicit negative evidence cases, real run-refusal proof for FAIL and UNAVAILABLE, stable JSON output, sentinel-secret leakage testing, non-mutation assertions, fitness checks, and Node-suite preservation. Recorded fixtures and local doubles are appropriate for this BIU; PY-10 owns real-target evidence.
material_risks: The doctor spans several adapters, so its result model and error classifier must remain uniform across predecessor interfaces.
A capability probe must not accidentally become a product mutation; local temporary-resource handling must be owned and cleaned up.

The current checkout is not a clean release baseline: main is ahead of origin by two commits and has one untracked document. This affects any claim about the exact current baseline, not the contract's readiness.
next_action: Create or advance the PY-09 BIU through the authorized work-management flow once PY-05, PY-06, and PY-08 are accepted; implementation may then use the stated contracts and verification requirements without new owner decisions.
rationale: SF-REQ-038 directly requires validation of installation, Work Management, provider, source-control, transport, lifecycle mapping, persistence, and execution capability before autonomous work. PY-09 covers each required extent, constrains it with FD-03-compatible fail-closed semantics and the established ownership boundary, explicitly excludes installer and broader product work, and leaves only normal adapter and test-design choices to implementation.

provider_evidence.note: reassessment after applying first-pass Agent-Ready findings
